item.title: Laura Clark: Reading resolutions courtesy of Theodore Roosevelt
item.description: The new year is almost upon us. Soon my social media timeline – perhaps yours as well, at least if you have particularly nerdy friends like I do – will be filled with New Year’s Resolutions centered entirely on reading.An avid reader myself, I love seeing reading goals from my friends. So let me take this time to encourage you to make some – then email me a list of your 2026 reading goals!For those who don’t know where to start, I suggest looking at Theodore Roosevelt’s autobiography for advice.

item.title: Alabama Independent Pharmacy Alliance calls for ‘further transparency’ of PBMs and health insurers
item.description: Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and health insurers should be subject to “further transparency,” according to the Alabama Independent Pharmacy Alliance (AIPA).Governor Kay Ivey signed legislation regulating PBMs into law in April. PBMs operate as intermediaries between drug manufacturers and insurance companies.AIPA was one of the groups that lobbied for the new law during the 2025 session. item.title: Montgomery apartment fire death toll now three
item.description: A pregnant mother is mourning the loss of her two children after an apartment fire in Montgomery.WSFA reported that an eight-year-old boy and a nine-year-old girl were killed in the fire at Woodley Terrace Apartments.The fire occurred Sunday morning. item.title: Bama comeback victory over Oklahoma in CFP the most watched first round game in expanded CFP
item.description: Last week's 17-point comeback victory over Oklahoma by Alabama in the College Football Playoff (CFP) marked the most-watched first-round matchup in the two years of the expanded 12-team field. According to ESPN and Nielsen, the Crimson Tide's 34-24 historic win over the Sooners in Norman, Okla., last Friday averaged 14.9 million viewers, making it the fifth-most-watched game of the season. item.title: UPS laying off 128 employees in Montgomery
item.description: UPS is laying off 128 employees in Montgomery, the company announced this week.According to an Alabama WARN List notice, the layoffs will begin on February 23.The layoffs appear to be part of UPS's nationwide downsizing.The Associated Press reported in October that UPS had cut 34,000 operational positions and closed daily operations at 93 leased and owned buildings nationwide.
